key_insight: Fully alloyed WC–Co–Cr powder enables dense layered coatings, while spray method strongly tunes the tradeoff between hardness and tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: The study helps select WC–Co–Cr coating processes for wear-critical machine parts by linking powder morphology and deposition method to coating quality and durability.
method: Compared detonation spray (DS) and HVOF deposition of WC–Co–Cr cermet coatings
Characterized powder and coating morphology with SEM and composition with EDS
Assessed microstructure, phase features, microhardness, and friction behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a harder DS coating with average microhardness of 1449 HV, while HVOF produced a dense, uniform coating with a low friction coefficient (Kt = 0.143).
watch_item: Results depend on the use of homogeneous fully alloyed powder, so performance may drop if powder morphology or spraying parameters are not tightly controlled.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
